_note: v6.3: the v6 ensemble recipe with both members upgraded: v10.3 (best CLIP model, validation HM 61.2%, test 66.3%) + aniq_baseline_independent_convnext_base (ImageNet-22k ConvNeXt-Base independent CNNs). Motivation: the two are strong on opposite sides. Calibrated, v10.3 gets unseen 83.3% but seen only 55.1%; ConvNeXt-Base (Hein's run: seen 67.0%, unseen 76.5%, HM 71.4%) is the strongest on seen pairs. v6 already showed the mix keeps the CLIP unseen accuracy while raising seen (v5 + ResNet-50: test HM 70.1% vs 65.1% / 59.7% alone). Members are put on log-probabilities over the 333 pairs and mixed as w * v10.3 + (1 - w) * ConvNeXt; w and gamma chosen on one validation split (seed 42, as v6-v6.2), where each member is retrained for its selected epoch count. Compare with v6.1 (v5.5 + ResNet-50, validation HM 58.9%) and with each member alone on the same split.
title: convnext_v10.3_ensemble

ensemble._note: Weight on the first member (v10.3) from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.1; w = 1 is v10.3 alone, w = 0 ConvNeXt-Base alone.

validation._note: Same split procedure, seed and settings as v5. gamma is in log-probability units here (both members are on the log-prob scale), so the grid is 0-15 in steps of 0.1; v5's 0.0725 cosine corresponds to 7.25.
